transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I'm here because I just can't stand how my face looks anymore, especially my skin. I have these awful, ugly scars and blemishes that make me look completely deformed, and it's all I can focus on.
How much time would you say you spend each day thinking about your skin and these scars or blemishes that bother you?

I easily spend several hours every single day constantly worrying about and analyzing my skin. It feels like these thoughts take up the vast majority of my day, and it's incredibly difficult to distract myself or make them stop.
Do you engage in any repetitive behaviors, such as excessive grooming, skin picking, or checking your appearance in the mirror, in an attempt to alleviate your concerns about your skin?

Yes, I spend hours checking my face in the mirror and constantly pick at my skin to try and smooth it out, even though it usually makes it look worse. I also spend a huge amount of time trying to cover up the flaws with makeup and grooming before I can leave the house.

Are your repetitive behaviors and thoughts primarily focused on your appearance and trying to improve or hide your perceived flaws, or are there other themes or concerns that also play a significant role in your obsessive thoughts and compulsive actions?

Yes, it is entirely about my appearance and trying to hide or fix what's wrong with how I look. I don't really have these kinds of obsessive thoughts about anything else; all my energy goes into checking the mirror, trying to cover up, and constantly comparing myself to others.

Have your concerns about your appearance and the resulting behaviors, such as excessive mirror checking and skin picking, significantly interfered with your daily routine, social relationships, or ability to work or study?

Yes, it has completely taken over my daily life. I spend hours checking the mirror, picking at my skin, and trying to camouflage it, which leaves me exhausted and constantly late for everything. I've become so self-conscious that I avoid seeing my friends and can barely focus on my work anymore.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms and behaviors, such as excessive preoccupation with perceived flaws in their appearance, repetitive behaviors like skin picking and mirror checking, and significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning, all align closely with the diagnostic criteria for Body Dysmorphic Disorder. The patient's focus is almost exclusively on their appearance and attempts to hide or fix perceived flaws, with no mention of other themes or concerns that might suggest other disorders. Given the comprehensive nature of the patient's symptoms and the significant impact on their daily life, Body Dysmorphic Disorder remains the most likely diagnosis, and no other candidates from the provided list are indicated at this time.
